name: Maria Gorlatova
title: Sternberg Family Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
department: Electrical and Computer Engineering; Intelligent Interactive Internet of Things (I3T) Lab
fitReason: Strong current applied-AI/HRI option with direct student-led physical systems and a separate public visiting-student inquiry route. Suitable projects could concern semantic grounding, robot interfaces or spatial AI, with concrete task scope and access negotiated before an eight-week visit.

physicalEvidence.summary: Full June 2026 fARfetch methods implement Grounding DINO, SAM and CLIP shared semantic mapping from robot/headset RGB-D, with GPT-4o adapting AR content. A real Unitree Go2 executes human-selected landmark goals and authored waypoints through SLAM Toolbox/Nav2; this is learned perception supporting physical navigation, not a new learned locomotion policy. The 13-person outdoor mock-inspection study includes 30.5 m separation and occlusion. It evaluates the integrated interface without component ablations or quantified VLM failure/latency analysis. A separate 2026 ARTOO-DARTU study uses YOLOv5/EasyOCR and an actual TurtleBot 4 in a 34-person controlled warehouse-like task; virtual targets do not establish physical item picking. Both are current Duke-group projects, with lead author Christian Fronk listed as the PI’s PhD student.

This supports contacting the lab about a visit, not confirmed admission, funding, eight-week availability or a summer 2027 opening.

unknowns: The outside-master classification, project fit, supervision, exact eight-week dates, on-site access, and remote possibility need explicit lab and Duke approval. A public invitation is not an acceptance or funding commitment.

Duke institutional guidance is reused from the completed 2026-10-01T01:15:42Z check rather than represented as newly verified. Visiting Research Scholars includes outside graduate students not taking Duke courses or receiving Duke salary; unit registration, work plan and compliance review are required before arrival. Paid arrangements may need a different appointment process.

The existing Duke visa guidance permits Student Intern visits up to twelve months and Short-Term Scholar up to six months, but the applicable category and eight-week appointment must be confirmed. Patient contact/care is restricted; a robotics-interface project should be scoped accordingly.

The reachable Duke J funding form accepts personal/family support but is internally dated 2023. Its $2,578 monthly figure is historical, not a verified 2026/2027 minimum. Current support amounts, insurance, all fees and lead time remain unresolved.

Physical claims are limited to observed implemented perception/interface-to-navigation systems. Human goals, conventional navigation and system-level evaluations are kept separate from autonomous learned motor control. The fARfetch headline percentage is not repeated because the reported mean times and its “66% faster” wording use an unclear comparison convention.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
